clue.text: Finishing off champagne with steak — making foremost amongst them question dish?

indicators.note: making one thing into another signals that a letter is swapped out for something else
finishing something off here means cutting away its final letter

parts.note: bubbles is an informal name for champagne, as the setter confirmed
with and and both mean together alongside
taken as written

indicators.note: the foremost of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of them
qu. is the standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: Someone polishing off the champagne with a steak, puzzling over what the meal is called.
explanation.walkthrough: The champagne loses its final S; in STEAK the T (first of 'them') becomes QU, giving SQUEAK. Bubble and squeak is a British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubble and squeak is a traditional British fry-up of leftover mashed potato and cabbage, so it is a kind of dish.

clue.text: Perhaps Harvey Nicks delivery expected — primarily with unopened flat pack

indicators.note: something unopened has had its opening taken away, so the first letter goes
primarily points to the first letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the initial letters of delivery and expected
a flat is an apartment
to pack away is to store

explanation.surface: A shopper at a smart London shop awaiting delivery of a self-assembly flat-pack.
explanation.walkthrough: Harvey Nicks is the nickname of Harvey Nichols, a luxury London department store; 'Perhaps' shows it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvey Nichols is a well-known upmarket London shop of exactly this type, so it is one example of the answer.

clue.text: Cleaning outfit — square's removing clothes covered in coffee

indicators.note: covered in means placed inside something else that wraps around it
removing clothes strips a word of its outer covering, its first and last letters

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
a hundred is the square of ten

explanation.surface: A prudish person stripping off while covered in spilled coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is a number here: ten squared is a hundred, which sheds its outer letters before sitting inside the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A launderette is a business where people wash their clothes, so it is literally an outfit that does cleaning.

clue.text: Touch on soap's conclusion being inspired by Dynasty — that is entertaining

indicators.note: to be inspired is literally to be breathed in, so one piece is drawn inside another

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: entertaining guests means holding them within, so this wraps around what follows

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its very last letter

parts.note: the final letter of soap

explanation.surface: A comment on how the ending of a TV soap took its cue from the 1980s series Dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Dynasty looks like the American soap, but it is the Chinese Ming dynasty; P goes inside MING, then I.E. surrounds the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To impinge on something is to encroach on or affect it, a sense close to touching on it.

clue.text: Clever person that set this up on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Fed is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The setter praising themselves for building a clue so neatly and punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person that set this' means the setter, whose pseudonym is Fed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means skilful and nimble, a close synonym of clever.

clue.text: Seeing threat demo posed — choppers maybe prepared for combat?

indicators.note: things that are posed are set out in a new arrangement, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
choppers is slang for teeth

explanation.surface: Helicopters readied for battle after a menacing show of force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choppers' suggests helicopters, but it is slang for teeth; the question mark flags that the teeth link the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed to the teeth is an idiom for being heavily equipped with weapons, ready for a fight.

clue.text: Welcome subject of discussion — ask if vote helped out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are scattered and put back in another order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A popular talking point: did a vote help someone out?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the phrase rather than defining it: people say it to greet someone who turns up just as they are being discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said in welcome when the person being talked about arrives, so it greets a subject of discussion.

clue.text: Half-hearted gospel minister's back on with a mass

indicators.note: on means placed after, setting the order of the pieces

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospels
W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of minister
M is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A clergyman going through the motions in his gospel reading and Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The minister's last letter is placed on, i.e. after, 'with a'; mass then ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm figuratively means lacking enthusiasm, the same as half-hearted.

clue.text: Swedish band regret turning record over the wrong way

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running in the opposite direction, right to left

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A Swedish band rueing a record that has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record over' is read as one unit and then reversed, after 'regret' has been turned on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is the Swedish rock group best known for 'The Final Countdown'.

clue.text: Get in boat at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb aboard a boat out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get in' reads as a phrasal verb, but only 'Get' is the definition; 'in' belongs to the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire it, a direct synonym of get.

clue.text: Nightwear's tight — good to go naked

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and a drunken word staggers into a different order
telling something to go means it is removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone whose pyjamas are too tight decides to sleep with nothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' seems to describe ill-fitting pyjamas but means drunk; the G is removed before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In the raw is an informal idiom for wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Live with Saint George?

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
St is the abbreviation for Saint

explanation.surface: A patriotic call to live under England's patron saint, Saint George.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint George looks like one name, but the clue splits after Saint: George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: George Best was a celebrated Manchester United footballer, so his surname completes the first name given, by example.

clue.text: Management helping to hold sledge back

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a ration is a helping or allotted portion

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a luge is a racing sledge

explanation.surface: Staff assisting with keeping a sledge from sliding away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb but is the noun for a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulation is the controlling or directing of something, which is a sense of management.

clue.text: Spots pub is hosting match

parts.note: your local is your nearby pub

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so the last word goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
a tie is a sporting fixture, a cup match

explanation.surface: A pub screening a football game on its television.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a cup tie is a knockout match; only 'is' holds it, not the whole of 'pub is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Localities are particular places or areas, just as spots are.

clue.text: Shocking treatment on board ship after discovering tiny woodworm, say

definitions.note: woodworm here is a plural mass noun, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind this one
dis-covering strips off the covering, the outer letters, keeping the inside

parts.note: the inner letters of tiny

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside it, so the treatment goes within

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a shock treatment

explanation.surface: A ship's crew horrified to find woodworm in the timbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like an adjective of outrage but is literal electric shock therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodworm are beetle larvae, so they are an example of insects; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Film Lyle's partner after hole in one

indicators.note: after means this piece comes behind the one named next

parts.note: an ace in golf is a hole in one
Tate & Lyle is a British sugar company

explanation.surface: A film about a golfer, Lyle, and his partner after a hole in one.
explanation.walkthrough: Lyle suggests the golfer Sandy Lyle, but the partner comes from the sugar firm Tate & Lyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a plastic sheet used as photographic and cinema film base, so it is a kind of film.

clue.text: Drunk son, crazy about the girl

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word encloses the next

parts.note: mad means crazy
she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: An intoxicated young man, wild about a particular girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Drunk looks like an adjective for the son, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed is slang for very drunk.

clue.text: His other Malbec keeps at constant temperature

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside, so the solution sits within these words

parts.note: runs across the words from the second letter of the first

explanation.surface: A man's second bottle of Malbec being stored at a steady temperature, like a wine cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Isothermal is the technical term for a process or state at an unchanging temperature.

clue.text: First Lady meeting resistance at all times

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A US president's wife always facing opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: First Lady suggests a president's wife, but here it is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever, as in 'ever ready', means always, at all times.

clue.text: Hardy girl just starting to embody essence of Geordie Shore

indicators.note: starting means this word comes at the front of the build

parts.note: but means just, as in 'he was but a boy'

indicators.note: to embody is to take into one's body, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is a Thomas Hardy heroine

indicators.note: the essence is the very heart of a word, its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of Geordie

explanation.surface: A tough girl starting out on the reality show Geordie Shore.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordie Shore is a British reality TV show set in Newcastle, whose natives are Geordies; but Shore is the definition, a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A shore is a prop that supports a wall, and a buttress does the same job, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Current terms of the Grand Unified Theory

indicators.note: a term is a limit or end point, so the final letters are taken

parts.note: the final letters of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A note on the present wording of physics' Grand Unified Theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as an adjective, up to date, but it is the noun: a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling current of water or air running against the main flow.

clue.text: Tom Petty originally heard round tent

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by how the letters are spoken, not how they are written
originally points to the first letter of each word, where each starts

parts.note: the initials of Tom Petty, said as two letter names

explanation.surface: The rock singer Tom Petty first heard playing around a campsite tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials are not used as letters but spoken, T and P, which spells the answer when written out.
explanation.definitionFit: A teepee is the conical tent of Plains peoples, circular at its base, so a round tent.

clue.text: For starters, Ratty and Mole regularly seeing Mr Toad drive aggressively

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of each of the words

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: The Wind in the Willows animals watching Mr Toad's reckless motoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty, Mole and Mr Toad are characters in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows; Toad is a famously reckless driver, but drive here means force through.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramrod something is to force it through forcefully, as with a rod ramming a charge home.

clue.text: Thrilling to pick most of cereal crop

indicators.note: most of means all but a little, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to elect is to pick or choose
rice is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A farmer delighted to harvest most of a grain crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric figuratively means exciting or charged with energy, as in an electric atmosphere.
